title: Admissible lattices in the square
statement:
Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{h}&Y\\
f\downarrow&&\downarrow e\\
S&\xleftarrow{g}&T
\end{array}
\qquad Y\simeq X\times_S T
$$
be a base-change square [sbc-def-base-change-square], with $f$ smooth
[def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension
$E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its ring of integers $A=\mathcal O_E$, and a uniformizer
$\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Assume that $T$ is
noetherian of finite dimension and $\ell$ is invertible on $T$, as required
for the integral and rational categories below.

For $n\geq0$ put $A_n=A/(\varpi^{n+1})$. On each corner $U$ of the square
write $(A_n)_U$ for the finite coefficient sheaf and
$\widehat A_U=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}(A_n)_U$. These are the coefficient
sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with its positive index
replaced by $n+1$. The finite coefficient sheaves are canonically the
constant ring sheaves, and use the inverse-image identifications of
[lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Use the integral full
subcategory $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and its raw rationalization
$\Dbc(T,E)=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)[1/\varpi]$ of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]; write $L[\varpi^{-1}]$ for the image of
$L$ under this scalar-localization functor.

An *integral lattice* for an object $K_E\in\Dbc(T,E)$ is a pair
$(L,\alpha)$ consisting of $L\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ and a chosen
isomorphism
$$
\alpha:L[\varpi^{-1}]\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E
\quad\text{in }\Dbc(T,E).
$$
The comparison with an idempotent-pair presentation in a Karoubi envelope
is a separate assertion, not part of this definition.

Define the reduction by derived extension of scalars along
$\widehat A_T\to(A_n)_T$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]:
$$
L_n=L\otimes^L_{\widehat A_T}(A_n)_T
\in D(T_{\Proet},A_n).
$$
In particular the integral tensor uses the completed coefficient sheaf,
not the constant sheaf associated to the abstract ring $A$.
The lattice is *finite-level etale admissible* if for every $n\geq0$
there exist $M_n\in\Dbc(T_{\Et},A_n)$ and an isomorphism
$\nu_T^*M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}L_n$ in $D(T_{\Proet},A_n)$.
Here the etale bounded constructible category is
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and $\nu_T^*$ is the derived
comparison inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Thus the
condition means membership in its essential image; it does not add
chosen witnesses to the lattice datum.

For any arrow $u:U\to V$ of the square, the subscript $n$ denotes
coefficients $(A_n)_U,(A_n)_V$, not a new morphism of schemes. The
functors $Lu_n^*$ and $Ru_{n,*}$ are the ordinary uncompleted derived
operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with the finite
coefficient identifications above. The lattice is *square-constructibly
admissible* if it is finite-level etale admissible and there exist integers
$a\leq b$ such that, for every $n\geq0$, all four objects
$$
\begin{aligned}
Rg_{n,*}L_n&\in D(S_{\Proet},A_n),\\
Lf_n^*Rg_{n,*}L_n&\in D(X_{\Proet},A_n),\\
Le_n^*L_n&\in D(Y_{\Proet},A_n),\\
Rh_{n,*}Le_n^*L_n&\in D(X_{\Proet},A_n)
\end{aligned}
$$
have constructible cohomology sheaves in the sense of
[def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and have
$\mathcal H^i=0$ for every $i\notin[a,b]$
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The same interval works for every
$n$ and every one of the four objects. No common stratification or
identification of these four families with reductions of integral
pushforwards is imposed by this condition.

statement_change.old_statement:
In a base-change square with $f$
smooth and $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and for
$E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and
uniformizer $\varpi$, an
*integral lattice* for $K_E\in\Dbc(T,E)$ is an object
$L\in\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$ together with an isomorphism

$$
L[\varpi^{-1}]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K_E
\quad\text{in }\Dbc(T,E).
$$

(The equivalence of this presentation with the classical presentation
by pairs $(L,e)$ with $e^2=e$ in the Karoubi envelope of the
rationalized category is the corresponding statement below.) The lattice is
*finite-level etale admissible* if each reduction
$L_n=L\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ lies in the essential image of
$\Dbc(T_{\Et},A_n)$; it is *square-constructibly admissible* if in
addition the finite-level systems
$Rg_{n,*}L_n$, $Lf_n^*Rg_{n,*}L_n$, $Le_n^*L_n$,
$Rh_{n,*}Le_n^*L_n$ are constructible in one common finite
cohomological interval.
statement_change.what: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported integral and rational constructible category symbols have no specified domain. In the existing constituent definitions they require T noetherian finite-dimensional with ell invertible. The identity square on Spec F_ell satisfies the imported geometric hypotheses but violates that category domain. State this domain explicitly on T; specify the completed coefficient sheaf, quotient indexing A/(varpi^(n+1)), essential-image functor, and the four object types. Keep the raw (L,alpha) lattice presentation and common interval from the master, without asserting the separate Karoubi comparison. The finite-dimensionality addition has an unresolved impact on the sole direct citer, recorded below.

citers.note: The four-system predicate and raw rationalization are unchanged, but the citer explicitly assumes only noetherian schemes and invertibility of ell, not finite dimension of T. Noetherianity alone does not supply finite dimension. Its category-domain hypotheses need review; independently, its exchange belongs on X although it prints S. The citer is not edited.
